title: Railway Restores Services for 5 Million Users After Security Breach
summary:
The cloud developer platform Railway has returned to normal operating capacity for its current users following a cyberattack that compromised stored environment variables. While services have been fully restored for the platform's 5 million existing users, the company has temporarily paused new signups to maintain system stability during the recovery phase.

The security breach potentially exposed credentials in roughly 100,000 workspaces, with Railway noting that attackers targeted AI API keys to conduct model distillation. The company stated it cannot refund customers for fraudulent AI token spending incurred through compromised keys, although it is assisting in escalating refund requests to those providers. Separately, an incident responder tracked a suspected attacker wallet moving approximately $371,000 in stolen cryptocurrency across 19 chains following the intrusion.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Railway’s services are fully restored for our 5 million existing users.
selectedTweets.text:
The security incident is resolved for existing users. We value transparency, and thus will continue to provide updates until all surface areas of Railway are fully operational.

Why is Railway still not accepting new signups?
Railway’s services are fully restored for our 5 million existing users. To securely and reliably support market demand, we have paused new signups as we prioritize uptime during this recovery period. We will reopen signups this week to continue supporting the ambition of product builders worldwide.

How can I get a refund for fraudulent AI spend on other platforms? 
Railway is unable to refund customers for spend performed with compromised API keys. However, we encourage you to reach out to AI token providers directly. Afterwards, please submit a support request at station.railway.​com with timestamps, prompts, and addition proof of fraudulent spend so we can escalate the request on your behalf. More information to follow.

What is Railway doing to improve security moving forward? 
This week, we have already or are actively implementing a new generation of builder, encryption, and logging systems. Railway has been acknowledged as critical cyber infrastructure, allowing us to utilize to previously inaccessible tooling to provide best-in-class security for our users.

Our goal has never been to simply get back to where we were. As more of the world's software gets built and run by agents alongside humans, security stops being one team's concern and becomes everyone’s ground floor. With these improvements, Railway will continue to be the best place for humans and agents to bring software to life.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Railway said a subset of users may be affected, yet it froze all deployments and reset bucket keys and GitHub tokens itself.
selectedTweets.text:
Developer platform Railway told every customer to rotate all secrets after an intruder decrypted some stored credentials.

Those environment variables hold database passwords, cloud keys and model API keys, letting anyone holding them sign in as the owner.

Railway said a subset of users may be affected, yet it froze all deployments and reset bucket keys and GitHub tokens itself.

It tied the intrusion to a string of attacks on platforms aimed at AI inference providers, and asked those providers to revoke keys.

Days earlier, OpenCode blamed a distillation attack for a breach possibly exposing OpenAI, Anthropic and Google keys saved by 1.4% of Console users.

Stolen keys let attackers harvest frontier-model answers for training rival models while victims pay the bills.
